subject: laavan warning: could not compute standard errors

parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to run a SEM using the lavaan package in R. The model will run and converges normally after 101 iterations. 

However, I get the following warning message:
"In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options = lavaanOptions,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!"

and so the summary does not provide standard errors and the corresponding p values for the parameter estimates.

I remember reading somewhere that this can happen with poor model fit - my model does not have great fit (chi squared p value = 0.024) but I've seen examples of other sems with much poorer fit that still have parameter estimate standard errors, so I'm not sure where I'm going wrong.

I've tried several things, including using group.equal="intercepts" or "loadings" and looking at the Modification Indices (for the latter I get another error message saying, 'system is computationally singluar: reciprocal condition number = 3.97448e-18).

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: laavan warning: could not compute standard errors
parts:
On 05/13/2013 03:26 PM, Natalie Clark wrote:
> Dear all,

> However, I get the following warning message:
> "In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options =
> lavaanOptions, :
> lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!"
This usually indicates that your model is not identified.

> model2<-'
> + # measurement model
> + WB=~Lifesat+Happy+Anxious+Worthwhile
> + Social=~TAHI+Qualification+Age
> + HGS=~GS_arealog+GS_diversity

Since you are using the lavaan() function (instead of cfa() or sem()),
you need to either fix the first factor loading to one, or fix the
factor variances to unity.

> > fit2<-lavaan(model2, data=bird, fixed.x=FALSE)

Yves.

Dear Yves,

Many thanks for your reply.

I first tried fixing the first factor loading of each factor to one but I still received the "could not compute standard errors" warning. Then I instead tried fixing the factor variances to one, and again received the same standard error warning.

I then tried both methods in the same model - fixing the factor loading of each factor to one and fixing the factor variances to one. This time, the model provided standard errors but the model indices (p-value of overall model, CFI, TLI and RMSEA) were all poorer than previous models which had no standard errors.

Is it OK to do both methods in the same model? Ie fix the factor loading of each factor to one AND fix the factor variances to one? Everything I've read suggests that you should only need to do one of those methods Is using both methods the reason I am receiving poorer model fit indices?

Many thanks and best wishes,

Natalie

On 06/03/2013 12:57 PM, Natalie Clark wrote:
> Dear Yves,
>

> Thank you for your continued help.
>
> I have tried running the model with the sem() function, using the below
> code:
>
> model<-'
> # measurement model
> WB=~Lifesat+Happy+Anxious+Worthwhile
> Social=~TAHI+Qualification+Age
> HGS=~GS_arealog+GS_diversity
>
> # regressions
> WB~Social+HGS+HGS_visits+LGS_visits
>
> # residual covariances
> Lifesat~~Happy
> Lifesat~~Worthwhile
> Happy~~Worthwhile
> GS_arealog~~GS_diversity
> HGS_visits~~LGS_visits'
>
> fit<-sem(model, data=bird, fixed.x=FALSE)
> summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
>
> However, the model still can not compute standard errors and I also get
> an additional warning about variance - "lavaan WARNING: some estimated
> variances are negative".

You have too many residual covariances. You can not correlate ALL
indicators of a factor (as you do for HGS). There is also no need to
correlate the exogenous predictors (and you can remove the fixed.x=FALSE
argument).

If you still have negative variances, you need to check you measurement
model first. Remove the regression, and make sure you have a good
fitting measurement model before you add the regression line.

Yves.
